crossRefs.note: Herodias set herself against him, and desired to kill him, but she couldn’t,
for Herod feared John, knowing that he was a righteous and holy man, and kept him safe. When he heard him, he did many…
It was now two days before the feast of the Passover and the unleavened bread, and the chief priests and the scribes…
For they said, “Not during the feast, because there might be a riot among the people.”
When they had further threatened them, they let them go, finding no way to punish them, because of the people; for…
Then the captain went with the officers, and brought them without violence, for they were afraid that the people might…
But if we say, ‘From men,’ we fear the multitude, for all hold John as a prophet.”
For John came to you in the way of righteousness, and you didn’t believe him, but the tax collectors and the…
The baptism of John—was it from heaven, or from men? Answer me.”
But if we say, ‘From men,’ all the people will stone us, for they are persuaded that John was a prophet.”

translations.web: When he would have put him to death, he feared the multitude, because they counted him as a prophet.
translations.bsb: Although Herod wanted to kill John, he was afraid of the people, because they regarded John as a prophet.
translations.kjv: And when he would have put him to death, he feared the multitude, because they counted him as a prophet.
